takeaways: Use standard Dataverse tables for core relational business entities and elastic tables, backed by Azure Cosmos DB, for high-volume operational data such as logs, telemetry and audit events.
Choose the partition key up front, ideally a hierarchical key with tenant ID at level one, and include it in every query to keep performance and tenant isolation intact.
Layer tenant isolation across Cosmos DB partitions, Dataverse business units and Power Pages table permissions, and push bulk ingestion to back-end services using CreateMultiple.
hook: Power Pages is usually dismissed as a portal builder, not a foundation for enterprise multi-tenant SaaS. This episode shows architects and Power Platform developers how Dataverse elastic tables, hierarchical partition keys and layered security make scalable, audit-ready SaaS on Power Pages possible, and where the approach stops being the right choice.
